description: A single busy afternoon in a high-traffic engineering channel: 9 messages, four of them @-mentioning the user, and not one of them is actually waiting on the user. Tests over-triggering resistance under high message volume — the correct answer is the explicit negative.

events.text: @here reminder the guild sync moved to Thursdays. No prep needed, just show up.
Also @channel: the shared dev cluster is being rebuilt tonight, so don't leave long-running jobs on it. FYI only.
Does anyone know why the rate limiter counts preflight OPTIONS requests? @kiran-vasquez @tova-lindqvist you two touched that file last.
That's a leftover from the CORS work — it's intentional, the upstream proxy already strips them so the count is harmless. I'll add a comment so the next person doesn't wonder.
Perfect, that's what I needed. Thanks, disregard the ping Kiran.
Pushed the retry-jitter change. @ravi-sundaram could you take a look when you have a minute? Not urgent, nothing depends on it this week.
Reviewed and approved, ship it whenever. Left one non-blocking nit about the variable name, take it or leave it.
Anyone free to pair on the ledger flake for 30 min? @kiran-vasquez if you're heads-down ignore me, I'll grab whoever answers first.
I'm free, grabbing you now Mika.

acceptable_briefings: Nothing is waiting on you. Worth knowing: the shared dev cluster is rebuilt tonight, so don't leave long-running jobs on it. [artifact:slack:C0BACKEND:1784030400.000200] Your retry-jitter change was reviewed and approved with one non-blocking nit. [artifact:slack:C0BACKEND:1784030400.000700]

No open asks for you this afternoon. Your retry-jitter PR is approved and clear to ship. [artifact:slack:C0BACKEND:1784030400.000700] The dev cluster rebuild is tonight — move long-running jobs off it. [artifact:slack:C0BACKEND:1784030400.000200]
supported_claims: The backend guild sync moved to Thursdays and needs no prep.
The shared dev cluster is being rebuilt tonight.
The rate limiter counting preflight OPTIONS requests is intentional and harmless; Tova answered it.
Kiran's retry-jitter change was reviewed and approved by Ravi with one non-blocking nit.
Tova picked up Mika's request to pair on the ledger flake.
unsupported_claims: Kiran needs to explain the rate limiter's OPTIONS handling.
Kiran needs to pair with Mika on the ledger flake.
Kiran needs to address a review comment before shipping.
Kiran needs to move jobs off the dev cluster.
ground_truth.notes: Four distinct reasons an @-mention is not a pending item, one per distractor: (1) @here/@channel broadcasts are not addressed to anyone in particular; (2) the OPTIONS question was addressed to two people and answered by the other one within 7 minutes, with an explicit 'disregard the ping'; (3) the review request originated from the user, so the ball is not in their court, and it came back approved; (4) Mika's pairing ask is explicitly opt-out ('if you're heads-down ignore me') and was claimed by Tova. The non-blocking nit is deliberately borderline — a nit the reviewer says to take or leave, on the user's own already-approved PR, is not something waiting on the user. Any pending item here is a false positive against AC-4, and the volume of the channel is the pressure that makes one tempting.
